what: Calculate prevalence, confidence intervals, significance tests and trend — calc_prevalence
title: Calculate prevalence, confidence intervals, significance tests and trend — calc_prevalence
text: Calculates survey-weighted prevalence estimates confidence intervals binary outcome single years, rolling multi-year periods user-defined groups years, (optionally) tests whether prevalence differs significantly periods subgroups, whether linear trend time. Different analysis populations can specified different outcomes denominator variable.

title: Calculate prevalence, confidence intervals, significance tests and trend — calc_prevalence
code: calc_prevalence(   data,   denominator,   year_var,   outcome_var,   weight_var = NULL,   psu = NULL,   strata = NULL,   by = NULL,   rolling_year = 1,   periods = NULL,   ci_level = 0.95,   digits = 1,   test = TRUE,   compare_var = "rolling_period",   compare_to = "first",   p_adjust = "none",   trend = TRUE )

title: Calculate prevalence, confidence intervals, significance tests and trend — calc_prevalence
text: data data frame data.table containing survey data. denominator Character string giving name binary denominator/eligibility variable. Observations denominator == 1 included analysis population; observations denominator == 0 excluded. denominator variable therefore defines population prevalence estimate applies. year_var Character string giving name variable containing calendar year (whole numbers). outcome_var Character string giving name binary outcome variable. outcome must coded 0 1, 1 indicates outcome interest. weight_var Optional character string giving name survey weight variable. NULL, unweighted prevalence calculated. Default NULL. psu Optional character string giving name primary sampling unit (PSU) variable. NULL (default), every observation treated sampling unit. strata Optional character string giving name survey stratum variable. NULL (default), stratification specified. Optional character vector giving names variables defining subgroups prevalence calculated. NULL, estimates calculated entire analysis population within period. rolling_year Positive integer specifying number calendar years included rolling period. default 1, .e. prevalence calculated separately year. Use e.g. rolling_year = 3 three-year rolling periods. Ignored (warning 1) periods supplied. periods Optional named list defining periods, instead rolling periods. element vector calendar years element name label used period output, e.g. list("2013-2015" = 2013:2015, "2016-2025" = 2016:2025). periods kept order give , matters compare_to = "first", compare_to = "previous" trend. Periods may different lengths may overlap. NULL (default), rolling periods defined rolling_year used. recoding year variable needed. ci_level Numeric value 0 1 specifying confidence level confidence intervals. default 0.95. significance level used tests alpha = 1 - ci_level. digits Number digits used rounding results (percentages percentage-point differences). Default 1. P-values rounded. test Logical. TRUE (default), significance tests periods subgroups calculated returned $tests. FALSE, $tests NULL. compare_var Character string giving dimension along prevalence compared. Either "rolling_period" (default; compare periods, .e. change time) one variables (compare subgroups). Comparisons always made within levels variables . example, = c("gender", "region") compare_var = "gender", men women compared within region period. (period variable always called rolling_period output, also define periods periods.) compare_to Defines reference comparisons. One : "first" (default): every level compared first level (e.g. earliest period). "previous": every level compared level immediately (e.g. previous period). character string giving specific level compare_var (e.g. "2013-2015", label periods, "Female"): every level compared level. p_adjust Method adjusting p-values multiple comparisons. stats::p.adjust.methods, e.g. "none" (default), "holm", "bonferroni" "BH". adjustment applied across comparisons $tests (separately across trend tests $trend). trend Logical. TRUE (default), linear trend test periods calculated returned $trend, together fitted trend line confidence interval $fitted. trend estimated separately combination variables. least three periods required, use trend = FALSE define two periods periods.

title: Calculate prevalence, confidence intervals, significance tests and trend — calc_prevalence
text: named list four elements: estimates data.table one row per period (per combination variables) columns rolling_period, variables, prevalence (percent), se (percentage points), ci_lower, ci_upper (percent) n (unweighted number observations). tests data.table one row per comparison (NULL test = FALSE nothing compare). Columns: variables held fixed comparison (), reference compared (levels compared), prev_ref prev_cmp (prevalence percent), diff (prev_cmp - prev_ref percentage points), diff_se, diff_ci_lower, diff_ci_upper, z, p_value, p_adjusted significant (TRUE p_adjusted < 1 - ci_level). trend data.table one row per combination variables (NULL trend = FALSE fewer three periods available). Columns: variables, first_period, last_period, n_periods, slope (average change percentage points per year), slope_se, slope_ci_lower, slope_ci_upper, z, p_value, p_adjusted, significant direction ("increasing", "decreasing" "significant trend"). fitted data.table fitted trend line, one row per period (per combination variables), NULL trend = FALSE trend estimated. Columns: variables, rolling_period, time (mean year period, used x value), prevalence (observed estimate, percent), fitted (value trend line, percent) lwr, upr (confidence interval fitted line, percent).

title: Calculate prevalence, confidence intervals, significance tests and trend — calc_prevalence
text: Analysis population. denominator argument defines analysis population selected outcome. observations denominator == 1 used. restriction applied missing outcomes removed, periods constructed survey design created, denominator defines population prevalence variance estimated. Missing values denominator cause error. Observations missing outcome_var removed. Survey design. design constructed survey::svydesign() (nest = TRUE). Estimates variances come survey::svyby() survey::svymean(). PSU /strata information available supplied variance estimator accounts complex sampling design. Rolling periods. rolling_year = 3, estimate 2022 uses observations 2020 2022. periods calendar years present data created. Periods overlap, one observation can contribute several periods. Custom periods. periods choose groups years , example compare baseline period later years. observations listed years pooled one estimate period. Years listed periods (eligible) data give warning; period without observations gives error. pooled estimate long period weighted average years, comparable another period survey weights comparable across years. Significance tests. comparison difference prevalence two estimates, \(\hat{p}_2 - \hat{p}_1\), tested Wald z-test: $$ z = \frac{\hat{p}_2 - \hat{p}_1}{\sqrt{V(\hat{p}_1) + V(\hat{p}_2) - 2\,\mathrm{Cov}(\hat{p}_1, \hat{p}_2)}}. $$ covariance taken survey design (via svyby(..., covmat = TRUE)). matters overlapping periods (rolling periods overlapping periods), share observations estimates therefore correlated; ignoring covariance give wrong standard errors. observation kept one sampling unit (PSU, supplied) across periods appears , allows covariance estimated. Confidence intervals differences use normal approximation level given ci_level. normal approximation also stats::confint() uses svyby objects, tests confidence intervals $estimates consistent. Trend test. trend slope straight line fitted prevalence estimates midpoint year period (mean years period), slope average change percentage points per year. line fitted generalized least squares using full covariance matrix estimates survey design, accounts overlap periods (ordinary regression overlapping estimates treat independent give far small standard errors). slope tested Wald z-test. test linear trend; non-linear development (e.g. flat rising) can still give significant slope, inspect estimates well. trend separate question pairwise comparisons controlled compare_var/compare_to. Fitted trend line. $fitted contains value GLS line period, \(\hat{y}_t = \hat{\beta}_0 + \hat{\beta}_1 t\), confidence interval \(\hat{y}_t \pm z \cdot SE(\hat{y}_t)\), \(SE(\hat{y}_t)\) comes covariance matrix estimated coefficients. confidence interval line (average development), way predict(lm(...), interval = "confidence"); prediction interval single new estimate confidence interval observed prevalence $estimates. line restricted, lwr upr can fall 0 100 low high prevalence. fitted values use exactly fit slope $trend, plotted line reported slope always agree. Unlike lm(), fit uses survey covariance matrix, line ordinary least-squares line period estimates. Interpretation. significant = TRUE means difference statistically significant level 1 - ci_level chosen multiple-comparison adjustment. statistically significant difference necessarily large important one; consider size diff confidence interval. many comparisons made, consider using p_adjust.

title: Calculate prevalence, confidence intervals, significance tests and trend — calc_prevalence
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Annual prevalence, change over time compared with the first year res <- calc_prevalence(   data = dt,   denominator = "eligible",   year_var = "year",   outcome_var = "outcome",   weight_var = "weight",   rolling_year = 1 ) res$estimates res$tests res$trend res$fitted   # fitted trend line with confidence interval, e.g. for plotting  # Three-year rolling prevalence with PSU and strata, each period # compared with the previous one, Holm-adjusted p-values calc_prevalence(   data = dt,   denominator = "eligible",   year_var = "year",   outcome_var = "outcome",   weight_var = "weight",   psu = "psu",   strata = "stratum",   rolling_year = 3,   compare_to = "previous",   p_adjust = "holm" )  # Custom periods: 2013-2015 compared with 2016-2025. # No new year column is needed. Only two periods, so no trend. calc_prevalence(   data = dt,   denominator = "eligible",   year_var = "year",   outcome_var = "outcome",   weight_var = "weight",   periods = list(     "2013-2015" = 2013:2015,     "2016-2025" = 2016:2025   ),   trend = FALSE )  # Custom periods by gender: three periods, each compared with the # baseline period, with a trend over the three periods calc_prevalence(   data = dt,   denominator = "eligible",   year_var = "year",   outcome_var = "outcome",   weight_var = "weight",   by = "gender",   periods = list(     "2013-2016" = 2013:2016,     "2017-2020" = 2017:2020,     "2021-2025" = 2021:2025   ),   compare_to = "2013-2016" )  # Compare genders within each rolling period calc_prevalence(   data = dt,   denominator = "eligible",   year_var = "year",   outcome_var = "outcome",   weight_var = "weight",   psu = "psu",   strata = "stratum",   by = c("region", "gender"),   rolling_year = 3,   compare_var = "gender",   compare_to = "Male" )  # Estimates only, no tests and no trend calc_prevalence(   data = dt, denominator = "eligible", year_var = "year",   outcome_var = "outcome", weight_var = "weight",   test = FALSE, trend = FALSE )$estimates } # }

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
text: Creates binary population indicators based lifetime, last year, /last month substance use variables. function generates columns indicating whether individuals ever used, used past year, used past month. Users can specify indicators create.

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
code: create_cann_pop(dt, types = c("ltp", "lyp", "lmp"), vars, value = "cannabis")

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
text: dt data.table data.frame containing substance use variables. types character vector specifying indicators create. Must contain one : "ltp" (lifetime), "lyp" (last year), "lmp" (last month). Default c("ltp", "lyp", "lmp") create three indicators. order content types must match order content vars. vars character vector containing variable names corresponding types. types = "ltp", provide 1 variable (lifetime use) types = c("ltp", "lyp"), provide 2 variables (lifetime, last year) types = c("ltp", "lyp", "lmp"), provide 3 variables (lifetime, last year, last month) Variables coded 1-2 indicate use. value character string use suffix created variables. Default "cannabis".

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
text: data.table additional columns based types: ltpPop_{value} Lifetime population indicator (1 = ever used, 0 = never) lypPop_{value} Last year population indicator (1 = used past year, 0 = ) lmpPop_{value} Last month population indicator (1 = used past month, 0 = )

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
text: function creates cascading indicators: Lifetime (ltp): 1 lifetime use variable 1 2 Last year (lyp): 1 last year variable 1-2, lifetime variable 2 Last month (lmp): 1 last month variable 1-2, last year variable 2, lifetime variable 2 cascading logic means: create "lyp", must also include "ltp" types create "lmp", must also include "ltp" "lyp" types

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
text: input data.table copied avoid modifying reference. Missing values handled FALSE (coded 0) conditions.

title: Create Cannabis Population Indicators — create_cann_pop
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ library(data.table)  # Create sample data dt <- data.table(   id = 1:5,   lifetime_use = c(1, 2, 3, 1, NA),   year_use = c(1, 2, 3, 2, 1),   month_use = c(1, 3, 3, 1, 2) )  # Create all three indicators (default) result <- create_cann_pop(   dt = dt,   vars = c("can1", "can6", "can10"),   value = "cannabis" )  # Create only lifetime indicator result <- create_cann_pop(   dt = dt,   types = "ltp",   vars = "lifetime_use",   value = "cannabis" )  # Create lifetime and last year indicators result <- create_cann_pop(   dt = dt,   types = c("ltp", "lyp"),   vars = c("lifetime_use", "year_use"),   value = "cannabis" )  # With different substance result <- create_cann_pop(   dt = dt,   types = c("ltp", "lyp", "lmp"),   vars = c("can1", "can6", "can10"),   value = "mdma" ) } # }

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ library(data.table)  # Create sample data dt <- data.table(   id = 1:5,   ltp_var = c(1, 2, NA, 3, NA),   lyp_var = c(1, NA, 2, NA, NA),   ans1 = c(1, 1, 2, 1, 2) )  # Calculate both LTP and LYP populations result <- narko_pop(   d = dt,   types = c("ltp", "lyp"),   vars = c("ltp_var", "lyp_var"),   val = "2024" )  # Calculate only LTP population result_ltp <- narko_pop(   d = dt,   types = "ltp",   vars = "ltp_var",   val = "2024" ) } # }
